definition: Environmental aesthetics is the study of how people perceive and find beauty, awe, or the sublime in natural surroundings. In this context, it focuses on how encounters with landscapes can shape meaning, values, and personal transformation.

reasons: The packet does not support the claim that environmental aesthetics is specifically the study of how people perceive beauty in natural surroundings; it only mentions an interdisciplinary understanding of environmental aesthetics in the context of awe and wilderness experiences.

The statement that encounters with landscapes shape meaning, values, and personal transformation goes beyond the packet’s support; the source mentions transformation, self-knowledge, and self-transcendence, but not values or a general theory of landscape-based meaning-making.
The packet does not provide a definition of “environmental aesthetics” or state that it is the study of how people perceive beauty/awe/the sublime in natural surroundings.

The packet only references an “interdisciplinary understanding of environmental aesthetics” in the context of a study of awe, the sublime, and transformation; it does not support the definition’s broader characterization as a general field of study.

The claims about “encounters with landscapes” shaping meaning, values, and “personal transformation” are only partially inferable (the packet mentions transformation themes and lifelong value/awareness), but they are not presented as part of an explicit definition of environmental aesthetics in the packet.
